subs.label: Comedy
subs.axis: Axis: by comic mode and engine (what makes the film funny): the clown and stage traditions first, then named national cycles, satire and dark modes, parody and performance forms, situational premises, youth and raunch comedy, crime and action hybrids, and comedy-drama by subject last.

leaves.label: Silent Clown Comedy
leaves.defn: A silent-era comedy (to c. 1930, plus Chaplin's late silents) built on the pantomime and stunt gags of a clown persona or on silent visual farce (The General, Safety Last!, The Kid, The Doll). A sound-era gag film in the same spirit goes to A12-3 Slapstick.
leaves.see: A12-3 Slapstick; A12-2 Comedian Comedy

leaves.label: Comedian Comedy
leaves.defn: A film built as a vehicle for a comedian's or comedy team's established persona, where the routines of the performer matter more than the plot (Duck Soup, The Bank Dick, The Gendarme of Saint-Tropez, Wayne's World, Billy Madison). If the film has a stronger premise engine (body swap, heist, parody) it goes there; a silent clown film goes to A12-1 Silent Clown Comedy.
leaves.aliases: comedian vehicle; comedy team film; double act (Steve Seidman's 'comedian comedy')
leaves.see: A12-1 Silent Clown Comedy; A12-3 Slapstick; A12-23 Parody & Spoof
leaves.axis: by the kind of comic persona the film is built around: team, Hollywood star comedian, national comic persona, sketch character, man-child

leaves.label: Slapstick
leaves.defn: A sound-era comedy whose main engine is physical and visual gag work: pratfalls, chases, destruction and choreographed mishap (Playtime, The Return of the Pink Panther, It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World, Bean), including the stunt-prank films of the Jackass line. A silent film goes to A12-1 Silent Clown Comedy.
leaves.aliases: physical comedy; visual comedy; gag film; stunt-prank comedy
leaves.see: A12-1 Silent Clown Comedy; A12-2 Comedian Comedy

leaves.label: Screwball Comedy
leaves.defn: A fast, dialogue-driven comedy of the 1930s–40s Hollywood type (and its later pastiches) in which a madcap heroine or eccentric pair upends social decorum, often across class lines (Bringing Up Baby, My Man Godfrey, The Lady Eve, Mr. Deeds Goes to Town). A divorce-and-reunion plot goes to A12-5 Comedy of Remarriage; a modern romantic comedy to A13.
leaves.see: A12-5 Comedy of Remarriage; A13 Romance

leaves.label: Comedy of Remarriage
leaves.defn: A screwball-era comedy whose plot is a married or divorced couple driven apart and brought back together (Stanley Cavell's canon: The Awful Truth, His Girl Friday, The Philadelphia Story, My Favorite Wife). Other screwball plots go to A12-4 Screwball Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-4 Screwball Comedy; A13 Romance

leaves.label: Comedy of Manners
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is the conversation, codes and hypocrisies of a social milieu, from Wilde and Lubitsch high comedy to modern urban talk comedies (The Importance of Being Earnest, The Women, Metropolitan, Hannah and Her Sisters, Pauline at the Beach). A plot driven by door-slamming mechanics goes to A12-7 Farce; open social attack to A12-15 Social Satire.
leaves.aliases: high comedy; drawing-room comedy; urban neurotic comedy; Comedies and Proverbs
leaves.see: A12-7 Farce; A12-15 Social Satire; A13 Romance
leaves.axis: by milieu and era of the talk: classical high society, contemporary urban circles, the neurotic New York comedy, the conversational moral tale

leaves.label: Farce
leaves.defn: A comedy driven by an accelerating mechanism of deception, mistaken identity, disguise and near-discovery, usually in a confined set (Noises Off..., The Dinner Game, Some Like It Hot, Housefull, Perfect Strangers). Talk-driven social comedy goes to A12-6 Comedy of Manners; bodily slapstick to A12-3 Slapstick.
leaves.aliases: bedroom farce; comédie de boulevard; comedy of errors; chamber comedy; cross-dressing comedy
leaves.see: A12-6 Comedy of Manners; A12-3 Slapstick
leaves.axis: by the farce mechanism: adultery and temptation, boulevard-stage plot, one-room chamber game, mistaken identity and doubles, cross-dressing disguise

leaves.label: Picaresque Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy that follows a roguish or innocent hero through an episodic string of adventures across a society, often a period or literary one (Tom Jones, The Decameron, A Dog's Will, Forrest Gump, Poor Things). A settled ensemble portrait goes to A12-57 Slice-of-Life Comedy-Drama.
leaves.see: A8 Historical & Period Film; A12-57 Slice-of-Life

leaves.label: Ealing Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy from the post-war Ealing Studios cycle (1947–57) of ironic, understated British comedies about little people and institutions (Kind Hearts and Coronets, The Lavender Hill Mob, The Ladykillers).
leaves.see: A12-43 Caper Comedy; A12-15 Social Satire

leaves.label: Commedia all'italiana
leaves.defn: An Italian comedy of the 1958–1980 cycle that laughs bitterly at national vices, sex, family and poverty (Big Deal on Madonna Street, Divorce Italian Style, The Easy Life, We All Loved Each Other So Much).
leaves.see: A12-14 Political Satire; A1 Movements & Schools

leaves.label: Comédia à portuguesa
leaves.defn: A Portuguese popular comedy of the 1930s–40s Lisbon cycle, built on neighbourhood types, fado and city-country contrast (The Courtyard of the Ballads, O Leão da Estrela, Aldeia da Roupa Branca).
leaves.see: A1 Movements & Schools

leaves.label: Bourekas Film
leaves.defn: An Israeli popular comedy of the 1960s–70s cycle built on Ashkenazi–Mizrahi ethnic stereotypes and mix-ups (Sallah Shabati, Snooker).
leaves.see: A12-27 Fish-out-of-Water Comedy

leaves.label: Mo lei tau
leaves.defn: Hong Kong nonsense comedy of Stephen Chow's type, mixing absurd non-sequitur, pop-culture spoof and cartoon violence (The God of Cookery, Kung Fu Hustle). A Hong Kong martial-arts action comedy goes to A12-49 Action Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-49 Action Comedy; A12-19 Surreal & Absurdist Comedy

leaves.label: Political Satire
leaves.defn: A comedy whose target is political power: rulers, regimes, campaigns, wars and churches (The Great Dictator, Dr. Strangelove, The Death of Stalin, Wag the Dog, Life of Brian goes to parody). Satire of class, lifestyle or media goes to A12-15 Social Satire / [[media]].
leaves.aliases: satire of power; war satire; religious satire
leaves.see: A12-15 Social Satire; A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire; A9 War Film
leaves.axis: by the power under attack: dictators and regimes, campaigns and governments, war and the military, religion

leaves.label: Social Satire
leaves.defn: A comedy whose target is a social order rather than a government: class, suburbia, consumer life, race, custom or the corporation (Life Is a Long Quiet River, American Beauty, Triangle of Sadness, Thank You for Smoking, Dear White People). Satire of media and show business goes to A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire.
leaves.aliases: class satire; suburban satire; corporate satire
leaves.see: A12-14 Political Satire; A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire; A12-6 Comedy of Manners
leaves.axis: by the social order under attack: class and wealth, suburbia and lifestyle, race, tradition and custom, corporations and advertising

leaves.label: Media & Show-Business Satire
leaves.defn: A satire whose target is the image industries: Hollywood, television news, celebrity and influencer culture, fashion and the art market (The Player, Network, The King of Comedy, Ingrid Goes West, Official Competition). A non-satirical backstage comedy goes to A12-32 Workplace Comedy; a fake documentary to A12-24 Mockumentary.
leaves.see: A12-32 Workplace Comedy; A12-24 Mockumentary; A12-15 Social Satire
leaves.axis: by the image industry targeted: film business, television and news, celebrity and influencer culture, fashion and art worlds

leaves.label: Black Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy that extracts laughter from death, murder, cruelty, taboo and misfortune, without a political or social target as its main point (Arsenic and Old Lace, Harold and Maude, Happiness, Wild Tales, The Banshees of Inisherin). Satire of institutions goes to A12-14 Political Satire / [[soc]]; crime plots played for laughs to the crime-comedy leaves.
leaves.see: A12-14 Political Satire; A12-45 Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy; A12-19 Surreal & Absurdist Comedy
leaves.axis: by what the darkness feeds on: death and corpses, murder, misanthropy and taboo, revenge and feuds, escalating nightmare

leaves.label: Camp & Trash Comedy
leaves.defn: A deliberately tasteless, low-budget comedy of outrageous excess, drag and bad taste celebrated as style — the John Waters line and its kin (Pink Flamingos, Female Trouble, Polyester, Pepi, Luci, Bom). Black comedy without the trash aesthetic goes to A12-17 Black Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-17 Black Comedy; A12-23 Parody & Spoof

leaves.label: Surreal & Absurdist Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy built on illogic: absurd premises played straight, dream logic, magical-realist fable or self-reflexive play with the film itself (Deerskin, Songs from the Second Floor, Arizona Dream, Adaptation.). Minimalist straight-faced comedy goes to A12-20 Deadpan.
leaves.aliases: absurdist comedy; surreal humour; metafictional comedy; anti-comedy
leaves.see: A12-20 Deadpan Comedy; A12-13 Mo lei tau; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde
leaves.axis: by the source of the illogic: absurd premise played straight, surreal or magical-realist fable, metafiction

leaves.label: Deadpan Comedy
leaves.defn: A minimalist comedy of expressionless performance, static framing and laconic timing (Drifting Clouds, Mystery Train, Divine Intervention, Whisky). Whimsical, designed indie quirk goes to A12-21 Quirky Indie Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-21 Quirky Indie Comedy; A12-19 Surreal & Absurdist Comedy

leaves.label: Quirky Indie Comedy
leaves.defn: An American-indie comedy of whimsical eccentrics, handmade design and wry melancholy, the 'quirky' sensibility of the 2000s (Napoleon Dynamite, Moonrise Kingdom, Lars and the Real Girl, Safety Not Guaranteed).
leaves.see: A12-20 Deadpan Comedy; A12-51 Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama

leaves.label: Cringe Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose laughter comes from social embarrassment and excruciating awkwardness sustained past comfort (The Foot Fist Way, Shiva Baby, Young Adult, Friendship).
leaves.see: A12-24 Mockumentary; A12-17 Black Comedy

leaves.label: Parody & Spoof
leaves.defn: A comedy that imitates the conventions of a genre, a specific film or franchise, a historical epic or a public persona in order to mock them (Airplane!, Young Frankenstein, Scary Movie, Monty Python and the Holy Grail, Zoolander). Spy spoofs go to A12-50 Spy Comedy; fake documentaries to A12-24 Mockumentary.
leaves.see: A12-50 Spy Comedy; A12-24 Mockumentary; A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire
leaves.axis: by the target imitated: a whole genre, a specific film or franchise, epic and historical drama, a public persona or milieu, television

leaves.label: Mockumentary
leaves.defn: A fiction comedy formatted as a documentary, or a staged 'real' encounter with a fictional character (This Is Spinal Tap, Best in Show, Borat, Zelig).
leaves.see: A12-23 Parody & Spoof; A19 Documentary

leaves.label: Sketch Film
leaves.defn: A comedy made of separate sketches or self-contained episodes, by one troupe or several directors (Monty Python's And Now for Something Completely Different, The Kentucky Fried Movie, Coffee and Cigarettes, Movie 43, Le Plaisir).
leaves.aliases: film à sketches; comedy anthology film; omnibus
leaves.see: A12-23 Parody & Spoof; A21 Short Film

leaves.label: Stand-Up Comedy Film
leaves.defn: A recorded performance of stand-up or solo comic monologue, released theatrically, on television or streaming (Richard Pryor: Live in Concert, Eddie Murphy: Raw, Hannah Gadsby: Nanette, Bo Burnham: Inside).
leaves.see: B15 Variety & Talk Formats; A19 Documentary
leaves.axis: by format: theatrical concert film, stand-up special, musical comedy special, solo monologue and stage show

leaves.label: Fish-out-of-Water Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is a character transplanted into a world whose codes they do not know: country and city, nation and culture, or class (Crocodile Dundee, Welcome to the Sticks, Trading Places, Legally Blonde, Local Hero). A transplant by magic goes to A12-28 Fantasy Comedy.
leaves.aliases: culture-clash comedy; immigrant comedy; rags-to-riches comedy
leaves.see: A12-12 Bourekas Film; A12-28 Fantasy Comedy
leaves.axis: by the border crossed: country and city, nation and culture, class and fortune

leaves.label: Fantasy Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy built on a single supernatural or magical premise whose consequences drive the gags (Groundhog Day, Freaky Friday, Liar Liar, Blithe Spirit, Doctor Dolittle). A technological premise goes to A12-29 Science Fiction Comedy; fantasy adventure to A6.
leaves.aliases: body-swap comedy; high-concept comedy; time-loop comedy; ghost comedy
leaves.see: A12-29 Science Fiction Comedy; A6 Fantasy & Adventure
leaves.axis: by the magical premise: body swap and transformation, wish curse or magic object, ghosts angels and the afterlife, time loop and time travel, talking animals

leaves.label: Science Fiction Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy built on a science-fiction premise (aliens, clones, inventions, apocalypse) whose consequences drive the gags rather than action (Coneheads, Multiplicity, Sleeper, Paul, This Is the End). Sci-fi action comedies go to A12-49 Action Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-28 Fantasy Comedy; A12-49 Action Comedy; A5 Science Fiction

leaves.label: Buddy Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is a pair or small group of friends or ill-matched partners and their friction (The Odd Couple, Twins, I Love You, Man, Romy and Michele's High School Reunion, The Hangover). A buddy pair of cops goes to A12-48 Buddy Cop Film.
leaves.aliases: odd-couple comedy; bromance; female buddy comedy; bachelor-party comedy
leaves.see: A12-48 Buddy Cop Film; A12-31 Road & Vacation Comedy
leaves.axis: by the bond: ill-matched odd couple, male friendship, female friendship, the bachelor-party pack

leaves.label: Road & Vacation Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy structured by a journey or a holiday away from home, its gags arising from the trip itself (National Lampoon's European Vacation, French Fried Vacation, Flirting with Disaster, Kikujiro).
leaves.aliases: road comedy; vacation comedy; holiday comedy
leaves.see: A12-30 Buddy Comedy; A12-35 Family Comedy
leaves.axis: by the trip: road journey, then holiday resort and vacation

leaves.label: Workplace Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy set in and driven by a workplace and its hierarchy, routines and colleagues (9 to 5, Office Space, Waiting..., Broadcast News, Day for Night). Satire of the corporation as such goes to A12-15 Social Satire; the military to A12-33 Military Comedy.
leaves.aliases: office comedy; backstage comedy; school comedy (teachers)
leaves.see: A12-15 Social Satire; A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire; A12-33 Military Comedy
leaves.axis: by the workplace: office and corporation, shops restaurants and services, newsroom and broadcasting, school (staff), hospital, show business and the arts

leaves.label: Military Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy of soldiers and military institutions: barracks and boot-camp service comedy, or farce set amid war (Stripes, Private Benjamin, Sgt. Bilko, La Grande Vadrouille). Satire of war itself goes to A12-14 Political Satire.
leaves.see: A12-14 Political Satire; A9 War Film

leaves.label: Sports Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy built on a sport or competition and the underdog struggle to win it (Caddyshack, Beerfest, The Big Year, The Cup).
leaves.see: A12-30 Buddy Comedy

leaves.label: Family Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is family life itself: parenting chaos, troublesome kids, in-laws, family gatherings and homes (Mr. Mom, Cheaper by the Dozen, Meet the Parents, Problem Child, The Flintstones). Family comedy-drama goes to A12-52 Family Comedy-Drama; children's films to A17.
leaves.aliases: domestic comedy; in-law comedy; live-action cartoon
leaves.see: A12-52 Family Comedy-Drama; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the family engine: parenting, the child, in-laws, the gathering, the house, cartoon families brought to live action

leaves.label: Wedding Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy organised around a wedding and its preparations, guests and disasters (Father of the Bride, Bridesmaids, Monsoon Wedding, The Wedding Ringer). A comedy whose aim is the couple's love goes to A13.
leaves.see: A13 Romance; A12-35 Family Comedy

leaves.label: Teen Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy of adolescent social life: high-school hierarchies, school pranks, summer camp and the one wild night (Ferris Bueller's Day Off, Clueless, Mean Girls, Superbad). Teenage sexual initiation goes to A12-38 Teen Sex Comedy; reflective adolescence to A12-51 Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama.
leaves.aliases: teen movie; high-school comedy; party movie
leaves.see: A12-38 Teen Sex Comedy; A12-51 Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the arena: high-school social life, the school as institution, summer camp, the party night

leaves.label: Teen Sex Comedy
leaves.defn: A teen comedy whose plot is the quest to lose virginity or to score (Porky's, Lemon Popsicle, American Pie, Blockers).
leaves.see: A12-37 Teen Comedy; A12-40 Sex Comedy

leaves.label: College & Fraternity Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy of campus life, fraternities and anarchic students versus the dean (National Lampoon's Animal House, Revenge of the Nerds, Old School, Neighbors).
leaves.see: A12-37 Teen Comedy

leaves.label: Sex Comedy
leaves.defn: An adult comedy whose engine is sexual desire, temptation and frankness, including its gross-out extreme (The Seven Year Itch, The 40-Year-Old Virgin, Deuce Bigalow: Male Gigolo, No Hard Feelings). Teenagers' quest goes to A12-38 Teen Sex Comedy; adultery mechanics to A12-7 Farce.
leaves.aliases: sex comedy; gross-out comedy; raunch comedy
leaves.see: A12-38 Teen Sex Comedy; A12-7 Farce
leaves.axis: by register: classic innuendo comedy, contemporary frank sex comedy, gross-out

leaves.label: Stoner Film
leaves.defn: A comedy built around cannabis or other drug use and the stoned perspective (Up in Smoke, Dude, Where's My Car?, Harold & Kumar, Pineapple Express).
leaves.see: A12-42 Slacker Comedy

leaves.label: Slacker Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy of aimless young adults hanging out, talking and avoiding work, including the low-budget mumblecore strand (Slacker, Clerks, Mallrats, Withnail and I).
leaves.see: A12-41 Stoner Film; A12-51 Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama

leaves.label: Caper Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy organised around a planned theft, swindle or escape, the plan and its unravelling being the engine (A Fish Called Wanda, The Sting, Dirty Rotten Scoundrels, Stir Crazy). Amateurs stumbling into crime go to A12-45 Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy.
leaves.aliases: heist comedy; con-artist comedy; prison comedy
leaves.see: A12-45 Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy; A2 Crime
leaves.axis: by the scheme: heist, con, jailbreak and prison

leaves.label: Gangster Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy set among professional criminals — the mob, gangland crews and hitmen (Analyze This, Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, Snatch, In Bruges). Civilians drawn into crime go to A12-45 Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy; hitman action vehicles to A12-49 Action Comedy.
leaves.aliases: mob comedy; mafia comedy; hitman comedy
leaves.see: A12-45 Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy; A2 Crime
leaves.axis: by the criminal world: the mob family, the gangland ensemble, the hitman

leaves.label: Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy
leaves.defn: A crime comedy in which ordinary people botch a kidnapping, robbery, killing or cover-up, the escalating mess being the engine (Ruthless People, Raising Arizona, Horrible Bosses, Delhi Belly). Planned professional jobs go to A12-43 Caper Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-43 Caper Comedy; A12-17 Black Comedy; A2 Crime
leaves.axis: by how the civilians fall into crime: a kidnapping, a get-rich scheme, a body to hide, being caught up by chance

leaves.label: Comedy Mystery
leaves.defn: A comic whodunit or detective comedy in which a mystery is investigated for laughs (Clue, Fletch, The Big Lebowski, See How They Run).
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery; A12-47 Cop Comedy

leaves.label: Cop Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy of bungling police, cadets and security guards as an institution, without the action-buddy formula (Police Academy, Super Troopers, Torrente, Paul Blart: Mall Cop).
leaves.see: A12-48 Buddy Cop Film; A12-32 Workplace Comedy

leaves.label: Buddy Cop Film
leaves.defn: An action comedy pairing two mismatched partners, at least one a cop, on a case (Beverly Hills Cop, Taxi, The Nice Guys, Let's Be Cops).
leaves.see: A12-49 Action Comedy; A7 Action & Martial Arts

leaves.label: Action Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose set pieces are action — chases, fights, shoot-outs, martial arts or sci-fi spectacle — played for laughs (Armour of God, Men in Black, The Hitman's Bodyguard, The Lost City). Cop pairs go to A12-48 Buddy Cop Film; spies to A12-50 Spy Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-48 Buddy Cop Film; A12-50 Spy Comedy; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by the action engine: adventure and chase, assassins, martial arts, sci-fi spectacle

leaves.label: Spy Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy built on espionage, either spoofing the spy genre or using spy action for comedy (Austin Powers, OSS 117, Johnny English, Charlie's Angels, The Spy Who Dumped Me).
leaves.see: A12-23 Parody & Spoof; A12-49 Action Comedy; A3 Thriller & Mystery
leaves.axis: by stance toward the genre: spoof, then straight action-spy comedy

leaves.label: Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama about growing up, from childhood through the first steps of adulthood (Amarcord, Juno, Frances Ha, Boy, Ghost World). Purely comic teen films go to A12-37 Teen Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-37 Teen Comedy; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by age of the protagonist: childhood, adolescence, young adulthood

leaves.label: Family Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama of a family's tensions and attachments, usually dysfunctional (The Royal Tenenbaums, Parenthood, The Farewell, This Is Where I Leave You). Comic family chaos goes to A12-35 Family Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-35 Family Comedy; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by the family bond in focus: the gathering, parent and adult child, siblings, the whole family in crisis

leaves.label: Marital Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama of a marriage under strain — affairs, divorce, therapy, the long haul (Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice, Heartburn, This Is 40, Hope Springs). Courtship goes to A13; remarriage plots to A12-5 Comedy of Remarriage.
leaves.see: A12-5 Comedy of Remarriage; A13 Romance

leaves.label: Midlife Crisis Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy or comedy-drama about middle and later life: the midlife crisis, retirement, ageing and late awakening (City Slickers, Sideways, About Schmidt, Grumpy Old Men, The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel).
leaves.see: A12-53 Marital Comedy-Drama; A12-55 Tragicomedy
leaves.axis: by life stage: midlife crisis, then old age and retirement

leaves.label: Tragicomedy
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama facing illness, grief, addiction or death, whose humour coexists with real loss (Steel Magnolias, 50/50, The Barbarian Invasions, The Bucket List).
leaves.see: A12-17 Black Comedy; A16 Drama

leaves.label: Ensemble Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama of a group of friends or a community whose interlocking stories carry the film, including the reunion film and the community underdog comedy (The Big Chill, Diner, Short Cuts, The Full Monty, Calendar Girls).
leaves.see: A12-30 Buddy Comedy; A12-57 Slice-of-Life
leaves.axis: by what binds the group: friends reunited, a community rallying behind an underdog project

leaves.label: Slice-of-Life Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A gently comic comedy-drama observing everyday life in a neighbourhood, town or creative milieu, with little plot engine (Marius, Smoke, Happy-Go-Lucky, Cutting It Short, The Horse's Mouth).
leaves.see: A12-56 Ensemble Comedy-Drama; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by setting: city and neighbourhood, village and small town, the artist's life

leaves.label: LGBTQ Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy or comedy-drama whose premise is queer identity — coming out, drag, queer family or a gay wedding (The Wedding Banquet, But I'm a Cheerleader, Breakfast on Pluto, Loose Cannons). Cross-dressing as disguise goes to A12-7 Farce.
leaves.see: A12-7 Farce; A12-51 Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama
